paper_summary: Mahesh (2025) fabricates epoxy (Lapox L12/K6) syntactic foams filled with 20, 40 and 60 vol% fly-ash cenospheres (CIL 100, SFC series) or recycled rubber crumb (CRMB60, SFR series) by room-temperature mechanical mixing and casting, and compares them with neat epoxy under ASTM D7136 drop-weight low-velocity impact at 39.62, 79.02 and 118.82 J. Rubber-crumb foams absorb the most total energy (SFR60: 16.75 J at 118.82 J impact vs 6.46 J for neat epoxy) via viscoelastic/ductile mechanisms, while the lower-density cenosphere foams give the highest specific energy absorption (SFC60: 0.0115 Jm3/kg, +117% over neat epoxy). Density falls from 1210 kg/m3 (neat epoxy) to 1005 kg/m3 (SFC60) but rises to 1630 kg/m3 (SFR60).

structure.microstructure_notes: Cast slab, filler sediments/floats through thickness giving a functionally graded distribution (cenospheres lighter at bottom, rubber crumb heavier at bottom). Absorbed energy 1.76 J of 39.62 J impact energy; SEA 0.0015 Jm3/kg (paper's own unit, not convertible to MJ/m3).

evidence.quote: NE | Impact 39.62 | Elastic 37.86 | Absorbed 1.76 | Density 1210 kg/m3 | SEA 0.0015 Jm3/kg
The neat epoxy samples show the lowest energy absorption, with values of 1.76 J, 4.77 J, and 6.46 J at the three respective energy levels.

The weight of the impactor assembly is 8.09 kg. The drop height is set to 0.5 m, 1 m, and 1.5 m, which corresponds to impact velocities of 3.13 m/s, 4.42 m/s, and 5.42 m/s ... Thus, the relative impact energies are 39.62 J, 79.02 J, and 118.82 J.

extraction_notes: 21 records = 7 compositions (NE, SFC20/40/60, SFR20/40/60) x 3 impact energies (39.62, 79.02, 118.82 J), all from Table 2. UNITS: the paper reports absorbed energy in joules and SEA in Jm3/kg (an unusual unit; SEA numerically equals absorbed energy / density in kg/m3). Neither maps onto the schema field energy_absorption_mj_m3 (MJ/m3), and the specimen thickness is not given, so no volumetric energy density can be computed. energy_absorption_mj_m3 is therefore left null and the joule values are recorded verbatim in test.specimen_notes and structure.microstructure_notes. Consequently no numeric Properties field is filled for any record - this paper reports no modulus, strength or strain data. Densities converted from kg/m3 to g/cm3 (divide by 1000). Volume fractions converted from percent to fractions. Cure/test temperature set to 25 C because the paper only states 'room temperature'. PARTICLE TYPE: only the SFC series contains hollow particles (fly-ash cenospheres). The SFR series uses solid rubber crumb, which is not a hollow-particle filler, so particle_type is set to 'other' for SFR and for neat epoxy (NE has no filler; particle_volume_fraction = 0). SFR rows are kept because the paper presents them as syntactic foams and they are the direct comparison set. DATA CONFLICT: Table 3 (CoR/ELP) mislabels rows - its 'SFR20' block carries Table 2's SFR40 numbers (3.56/7.08/13.98 J) and its 'SFR40' block duplicates SFC60's numbers (3.31/10.73/11.54 J). Table 2 is internally consistent and is corroborated by the running text (SFR20 = 9.45 J at 118.82 J, Sec. 3.4), so all values were taken from Table 2. Coefficient of restitution and energy-loss percentage have no schema field and were not extracted. Gradation-test layer weights (Figures 7a/7b) are only shown in figures and are not reported numerically per layer, so no per-layer records were created.
